name: RULER
intro: RULER基准扩展了传统的needle-in-a-haystack测试，旨在全面评估长上下文语言模型。它支持灵活配置序列长度和任务复杂度，涵盖多种“针”（信息）的类型和数量，并引入了多跳追踪与聚合等新任务，用以测试模型超越简单信息检索的行为能力。
task_type: 开放式问答, 分类, 补全
intro_en: The RULER benchmark extends the traditional needle-in-a-haystack test to comprehensively evaluate long-context language models. It supports flexible configuration of sequence length and task complexity, covers various types and quantities of "needles" (information), and introduces new tasks like multi-hop tracking and aggregation to assess models' abilities beyond simple information retrieval.

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-18; status=source-reconstructed-awaiting-independent-signoff. Primary evidence: RULER, arXiv:2404.06654v3, published at COLM 2024. The reviewed PDF SHA256 is 8a4bc6ca28d84570eec7f42652400c2121f4c8bc361701634e596772e396fc22. The paper-era official repository snapshot is dbc6a83c2f60d034dfaab8e7af42dde1a5d2e3dc dated 2024-08-01; the separately audited current official head is 38da79d79519ef87aa46ae804f838e1eab7f86d7 dated 2026-06-25. Construction contract: RULER automatically generates configurable long-context examples by setting sequence length and task complexity, where complexity changes target-output volume and signal-to-noise ratio. Four behavior categories are preserved. Retrieval contributes eight of the 13 representative configurations: three S-NIAH settings, three MK-NIAH settings, one four-value MV-NIAH, and one four-query MQ-NIAH. The S-NIAH configurations cover repeated-noise passkey retrieval, essay-background vanilla NIAH, and UUID-value robustness; MK-NIAH covers four keys plus the line-retrieval and key-value-retrieval full-needle haystacks. Multi-hop tracing contributes one variable-tracking configuration with one chain, four bindings, and five variable names to return. Aggregation contributes CWE with ten common words appearing 30 times versus uncommon words appearing three times, and FWE with Zeta alpha 2.0 and top-three frequent-word output. Question answering contributes SQuAD single-hop and HotpotQA multi-hop configurations, extending their gold paragraphs with distractor paragraphs sampled from the same dataset. The paper selects these 13 configurations after a task-correlation study, rather than treating every combinatorial configuration as part of the headline suite. Generation and evaluation contract: the selected task suite, the 4K, 8K, 16K, 32K, 64K, and 128K length grid subject to each model's supported context, and the applicable model-plus-task prompt templates jointly determine generation. For every selected task-length pair, the paper generates 500 evaluation examples. A task template supplies instruction, context, and query, the model chat template wraps them, and a task answer prefix is appended. Only VT and CWE receive one in-context demonstration; the other task routes do not. The applicable prompt route, including that demonstration where used, is assembled before the generator is invoked and is counted in the sequence-length budget. Direct-answer or no-explanation wording is task- or model-template-specific, explicitly appearing in only some templates, and is not generalized to the entire non-VT/CWE route. The experiment covers 17 long-context language models: 15 open-source models plus GPT-4 and Gemini-1.5. The paper prose reports vLLM inference in BF16 on eight A100 GPUs and greedy decoding across the experiment. The paper-era snapshot is narrower: config_models.sh explicitly configures Llama2-7B-Chat via vLLM, GPT entries through the OpenAI API wrapper, and Gemini entries through the Gemini API wrapper; it does not enumerate all 15 open-source models as vLLM entries. This is a scope discrepancy between the blanket paper prose and the explicit implementation entries, so the graph presents both facts without projecting one configured local-model route onto all 15 open-source models. Scoring checks for the target output with recall-based accuracy. Per-length model performance is the mean across the 13 tasks; increasing and decreasing length-weighted averages are also reported. Effective context length is the greatest tested length exceeding 85.6%, the Llama2-7B score at 4K, and is compared with claimed context length. Version boundary: dbc6a83c2f60 is used only to corroborate the paper-era 13 names, configuration implementation, and OpenAI/Gemini API routing. The current 38da79d79519 tree includes 2025 generator corrections, later QA and length-generation fixes, and guidance to a RULERv2 branch; those changes are explicitly separated from the COLM 2024 workflow. Release boundary: examples are generated from configurations, and the paper reports 500 per task-length pair rather than an immutable row-level train/dev/test snapshot. License boundary: the official repository carries Apache-2.0 for its code snapshot. The specs use solid arrows only for the construction and evaluation path and dashed arrows for source, release, implementation-version, drift, and license boundaries. English and Chinese graphs have identical node IDs, types, sizes, positions, styles, edge tuples, and branch geometry, with no edge labels. This is source-stage evidence only. strict Draw.io/XML and runtime visual review are required next; formal assets and page fallbacks remain gated until independent reviewer approval. Existing formal drawio, arch, SVG, and PNG outputs were not regenerated in this step and are not cited as signoff evidence.
